title: Test and release the whole service
outcome: Run a release rehearsal with real requests and a tested rollback.
story: Amina will depend on your system tomorrow morning. Before making it available, prove that its important paths work and that you can recover a failed release.

frames.explanation: A green code test is only one part of a release.
A release needs a working recovery path as well as a happy path.

sections.title: Choose tests for the boundaries
paragraphs: A unit test checks a small rule such as quote. An integration test checks connected parts such as an endpoint, session, and database. A browser test checks what a person can do in the interface.

Use a few meaningful flows: sign in, create a message, retrieve it, deny another customer, and preserve a failed draft. Test both status and stored data. A mocked repository test alone cannot prove that the SQL and endpoint are connected correctly.

sections.title: Separate environments
paragraphs: Use disposable data for tests and local practice. Put environment-specific configuration in server variables. Keep real credentials out of the frontend bundle and repository.

Pin dependency versions and record the runtime version. Build the frontend from a clean checkout. A deployment package should be repeatable, so a teammate can reproduce what was released instead of relying on files left on your machine.

sections.title: Release with a checklist you can prove
paragraphs: Before deployment, run tests, rehearse migrations on a copy, verify required configuration, and check the service health endpoint. Health should communicate whether the service is ready to accept work, including the database dependency.

A green status is evidence only if the underlying check actually ran. The browser exercise plans a gate; it does not deploy. The project records command outputs, an HTTP smoke test, and a database reopen check.

sections.title: Practice rollback before an incident
paragraphs: Keep the previously working application version and a verified database backup. Document whether a migration is reversible; rolling back code alone may not undo a changed schema.

Rehearse recovery locally with a deliberate failing version. Restore the intended version and data, then repeat the main smoke flow. Do not declare recovery because a process starts: prove that a customer can complete the operation.

words.meaning: A test of multiple connected parts working together.
A small check that the most important released behaviour works.
Returning to a verified earlier version after a failed change.

explanation: The checks have a deliberate order.
The first failed or missing check stops the gate.
Ready is returned only when every required check has evidence.

exercise.title: A release decision
exercise.brief: Write release(checks). Check tests, migration, config, health, rollback in that order. Missing or false values stop with stop:name; all true returns ready.

steps.title: Require passing tests
steps.task: Stop with stop:tests when tests is false or missing.
steps.hint: Use checks.get("tests") so a missing result also stops.
steps.solution:
def release(checks):
    return "ready" if checks.get("tests") else "stop:tests"

steps.title: Verify data and configuration
steps.task: After tests, require migration and config in that order.
steps.hint: A loop can avoid repeating the same condition.

steps.title: Verify operation and recovery
steps.task: Finally require health and rollback. Fail closed on missing evidence.
steps.hint: Extend the ordered list; do not use a default of True.

cases.label: Tests failed
cases.why: Broken behaviour cannot pass the gate.

cases.label: Every check verified
cases.why: A complete set of evidence permits review.

cases.label: Migration unverified
cases.why: Stored data needs its own check.

cases.label: Configuration missing
cases.why: A build may fail with wrong deployment settings.

cases.label: Service is unhealthy
cases.why: A running process is not always ready.

project.title: A full-stack release rehearsal
project.brief: Release the local shop workspace from a clean checkout. Use the included Docker option or documented local commands, and rehearse a failure and recovery.
deliverables: A rollback rehearsal with a smoke-test result.

milestones.title: Run connected tests
actions: Test sign-in, create, list, and denied access.
Exercise the connected frontend in a browser.

milestones.title: Build a reproducible release
actions: Build the frontend and start the service.
Check health and a real create-message request.

milestones.title: Recover a deliberate failure
actions: Introduce a harmless local failure, restore, and repeat the smoke test.

acceptance: The build starts from documented commands.
No private configuration enters the frontend bundle.
The rollback restores a usable service and intended data.

tests.expected: Health or requests report failure accurately.
The verified version serves the main flow again.

project.extension: Add a CI job that runs these checks and retains a safe failure report. Document which checks still require a human rehearsal.
reflection: Which boundary did each test cover?
What did your health check actually prove?
What would code rollback leave unchanged in the database?
